title: Everything we know about the Louvre jewellery heist
facts: Thieves wielding power tools broke into the Louvre Museum in Paris during broad daylight and stole eight items of jewellery. [cite: 256]
Four suspects utilized a vehicle-mounted mechanical lift to access the Louvre's Galerie d'Apollon via a balcony. [cite: 256]
Two of the thieves entered the Louvre Museum by cutting through a first-floor window using power tools. [cite: 256]
The thieves cut through the glass of two display cases inside the Louvre Museum to steal the jewels. [cite: 256]
French police reported the thieves remained inside the Louvre Museum for four minutes before escaping on two waiting scooters at 09:38 local time. [cite: 256]
A preliminary report indicated that one in three rooms in the raided area of the Louvre Museum lacked CCTV cameras. [cite: 256]
The French culture ministry stated that the Louvre museum's wider alarms activated during the burglary. [cite: 256]
A museum staff member intervened to prevent the thieves from setting fire to their vehicle outside the Louvre. [cite: 256]
Approximately 60 investigators were assigned to work on the Louvre Museum theft case. [cite: 256]
The eight stolen items from the Louvre Museum include 19th-century diadems, necklaces, ear-rings, and brooches. [cite: 256]
Empress Eugénie's crown was discovered damaged on the thieves' escape route after apparently being dropped. [cite: 256]
Louvre officials requested government assistance earlier in the year to restore aging exhibition halls and enhance artwork protection. [cite: 256]
French President Emmanuel Macron pledged to redesign the Louvre Museum as part of the New Renaissance project costing between 700 million and 800 million euros. [cite: 256]
Thieves broke into the Adrien Dubouche Museum in Limoges in September 2025 and stole porcelain works valued at 9.5 million euros. [cite: 256]
Armed robbers raided the Hieron Museum in Burgundy in November 2024 and stole 20th-century artworks. [cite: 256]
